t: Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States to the United States courthouse referred to in section 1 shall be deemed to be a reference to the “Paul Brown United States Courthouse”.

fable.w: This is a boilerplate naming provision that deems existing references to a courthouse to refer to its new name. The tempting reading is that the word "regulation" signals rulemaking, but here it only lists a type of record in which the old name might appear; it does not authorize or require any rule. No party outside the federal government is consulted or given any role in a federal decision.
fable.s: Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States

opus.w: This is a standard naming provision. It says that references to the courthouse in federal records should be read as the new name. The mention of 'regulation' only lists record types; it does not give anyone authority to make rules. No outside party is consulted, heard, or given a role in any federal decision.
opus.s: Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States to the United States courthouse referred to in section 1 shall be deemed to be a reference to the “Paul Brown United States Courthouse”.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The word "regulation" appears, which might suggest rulemaking. That fails here. The word only appears in a list of records that must treat the new courthouse name as the official one. Nothing authorizes or requires rulemaking, and no one outside the federal government is involved in any decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a purely administrative directive regarding the naming convention for a federal building in official records. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or interaction with parties outside the federal government. There is no advisory board, public comment period, or requirement to consult with states, tribes, or the public.
qwen_chat.s: Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States to the United States courthouse referred to in section 1 shall be deemed to be a reference to the “Paul Brown United States Courthouse”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that renaming a building involves public input or consultation, but the text itself contains no such requirement. It is purely a directive on how to interpret references in official records.
